tei:titleStmt.tei:title: שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרִיתוֹת
Shlōsh Esréh Britōt — a shiv'ata cycle for Musaf on the Shabbat of a bar mitsvah, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:div.tei:head: Shlōsh Esréh Britōt — a shiv'ata cycle for Musaf on the Shabbat of a bar mitsvah, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:lg.tei:l: Thirteen covenants the father of multitudes accepted upon his children:
circumcision, the cheer of Torah, and the joy of marriage.
On this one’s bar mitsvah, shield, o Guardian of Faith,
the guarded generation; let it grow under shields.
Blessed are You, Cause, Shield of Abraham.
You are mighty...
Thirteen attributes of compassion You taught to the one drawn from water,
and You swore that gracious dew You would precipitate from heaven.
On this one’s bar mitsvah, remember this male like Menasseh and Ephraim.
strengthen him with dew of heavenly light!
Blessed are You, Cause, who revives the dead.
Ashkenaz: Let’s exult in You... Sefarad: A crown...
Thirteen theses are engraved in the law of Israel.
Magnified and praised be the living God, the Redeemer!
On this one’s bar mitsvah, confirm him to fulfil ten in Ariel,
To add to the three holinesses of Israel!
Blessed are You, Cause, the holy God (on Shabbat Shuva: Sovereign)
You established...
Thirteen principles spoke the greatest of the Tannaim,
by which the Torah is interpreted, as well as written scriptures.
On this one’s bar mitsvah, he relies on You — along with all comers,
the people keeping the sabbath and calling it a delight.
Blessed are You, Cause, who sanctifies the sabbath.
Desire...
Thirteen gates, openings of the Courtyard;
the righteous bowed prostrate there in might.
On this one’s bar mitsvah, he has taken up the yoke and light of the Torah.
Desire our prayers, and we will worship You in awe!
Blessed are You, Cause, who returns Their presence to Ẓíōn.
We thank...
Thirteen shofars, tables, and prostrations corresponding,
as such our tradition was passed on to us by their hand.
On this one’s bar mitsvah, every human relies on You.
Thanks we thank, and to You we bow, their Rock and Foundation!
Blessed are You, Cause, whose name is good, to You it is pleasing to praise.
Grant...
Thirteen years Ẓíōn’s children arrive to adulthood.
The righteous established it, engraved on tablets.
On this one’s bar mitsvah, the divine portion of Abraham and Ruth
this friend of Yours will accept, peace, satistfaction, and freedom!
Blessed are You, Cause, who blesses Their people Israel in peace.

tei:note.tei:p: Mishnah Nedarim 3:11. In Genesis 17. the word “covenant” appears thirteen times.
According to Genesis 48:20, the people Israel should be blessed by being compared to these two sons of Joseph.

First listed in Rambam’s commentary on Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:1, but brought into the post-service recitations as a “credo” of rabbinic Judaism, and rewritten in to the piyyuṭ Yigdal recited, in many communities, at the end of every Friday night service.
Once reaching bar mitsvah age, a child can be counted in a minyan.
A poetic term for Jerusalem, found in Isaiah 29:1
”Three holinesses” refers to the threefold repetition of “holy” in Isaiah 6:3. And ten plus three is, of course, thirteen.
First listed in the opening of the Sifra, the thirteen hermeneutical principles of Rabbi Ishmael are recited every morning in traditional liturgies.

Rabbi Ishmael ben Elisha’s system of halakhic exegesis became the norm by which all halakha was derived, and he was also an expert in aggadah. His school of students, Bei Rabbi Yishmael, brought down many important teachings. Only Rabbi Akiva reached his level of importance in his generation.
See the Yism’ḥu text, recited as part of the sabbath service — in Ashkenaz practice exclusively as part of Musaf, and in Sephardi practice as part of every service.
Of the Temple courtyard, listed in M. Shekalim 6:3
A line from the old Erets Yisrael conclusion of this prayer.
Both of whom accepted the Torah by their own choice, rather than having been obligated into it since birth.
